title: an idle queue worker asks its queue once a second, and a push in the same process wakes it once the job is committed
scope:
how long a `[queue]` worker waits after it finds no due job, and what ends that wait
early. It does not change the claim, the write-back, the retry ladder or the visibility window of
[0084](0084.md), it does not change which process runs a job ([0154](0154.md)), and it adds no
`[queue]` key.
dependsOnText:
[0084](0084.md) (a job is a row, and a push commits with its caller's transaction),
[0154](0154.md) (the workers run inside `nvs serve`, and the drain stops them), [0229](0229.md) (a
task may take a wake handle for one wait and let it go).
validatedBy:
the cases under *Verification* in `crates/nvs-cli/src/worker.rs`,
`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/db/transaction.rs`, `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/queue/bell.rs` and
`crates/nvs-runtime/src/ctx/held.rs`, and the measurement there.

summary.headline: An idle queue costs almost nothing
summary.body:
A queue worker with no job used to check the database a hundred times per second. It now
checks once per second. A job that the same process adds still starts at once, because
`Core\Queue::push` wakes the workers when the job is saved. Inside a transaction, the workers are
woken when the transaction commits. A job that another process adds, a job with a `runAt` time
and a job that runs again after an error can start up to one second late.
